```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Both ideas enter crowded markets, but A's buyers are an enumerable universe of municipal governments with a legal obligation (WCAG 2.1 AA under the DOJ Title II rule). That lets a solo operator do direct, targeted outreach. B depends on being discovered in an App Store category where incumbents already hold 100–473 reviews.",
    "A has sourced, bounded acquisition costs: $1,300–$1,800 conference booths and $250–$7,500 league sponsorships. These give direct access to decision-makers inside 90 days. B's only sourced paid channel says about $500/month must be sustained for 90 days before payback data even emerges, which uses up the whole window before any signal arrives.",
    "A's published price points ($29–$349/mo) sit under the micro-purchase threshold, so a single budget holder can buy without an RFP. B's entry pricing has been pushed to $5–$12.90/mo, and its dominant incumbent (473 reviews, 4.9 stars) offers a free plan. That makes a first paid conversion harder to win against free alternatives.",
    "The deadline extension weakens A's urgency but does not remove it. Large entities still face an April 2027 deadline. A new entrant can also stand out by using the correct dates, since several competitors' sites still show the stale April 2026 date.",
    "B's brief names concrete support and quality risks for a one-person shop: Describly sits at a 1.0 rating after a billing failure, and AltText.ai has a 5% one-star rate. It also flags possible technical inferiority of photo-only input. A's comparable risk, liability from overselling automated scans, can be reduced by how the product is positioned."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence rests on two Reddit threads, one of which, judging by its URL ID (8if023), looks several years old, plus a review of a competitor's app. These show that the pain existed, not that it is unmet today. The brief's own evidence suggests incumbents have already absorbed it, with one free app holding 473 reviews. The 'industry commentary' about photo-only input being inferior carries no source and counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A's demand evidence is also thin. It consists of one industry quote about deadline difficulty, an NLC survey showing uncertainty rather than willingness to pay, and a vendor-sourced marketing claim that should be discounted. The brief provides no free-scan-to-paid conversion data and no CPC data, and says 6–7 near-identical competitors are already in a price war. The deadline extension may also slow purchasing. A wins mainly because its acquisition path and buyer targeting look more feasible within 90 days, not because its demand is well proven."
}
```
